articleTitle: Effect of Crystal Orientation on Vertical Coercivity in Co-Cr Film
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A higher perpendicular coercivity is needed if Co-Cr film is to deliver a higher reproduced output. In this paper, we report on a means of obtaining Co-Cr film on PET substrates with a high perpendicular coercivity. A low degree of crystal orientation in the Co-Cr film results in a high perpendicular coercivity. In double layer media, the crystal orientation of the Co-Cr layer changes with that of the permalloy underlayer. A high reproduced output was obtained at densities up to 100 kBPI using Co-Cr/permalloy double-layer media with high perpendicular coercivity in the Co-Cr layer and a single pole head. The inclination of the easy axis in a simple magnetic wall motion model or a magnetization rotation model cannot explain the increase in perpendicular coercivity. Possibly the degradation of the orientation of the Co-Cr film acts to increase the Cr segregation, resulting in a larger perpendicular coercivity.

articleTitle: Multi-Ability Sensor Module Using a Temperature-Sensitve Magnetic Semiconducter with Humidity Dependence
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The temperature-sensitive magnetic semiconductor (TMS) is a multifunctional sensor with thermistor and thyratron-type bidirectional diode functions in a temperature-sensitive magnetic core. In the TMS, capacity and resistance are humidity dependent and they decrease with rising humidity. The temperature dependence of the magnetic reluctance is independent of humidity. The current-voltage characteristics show a bidirectional non-linear conduction phenomena which covers three states; a cut off state, a negative resistance state and an on state. The application of the TMS for utilization as a versatile temperature/humidity measurement module is shown.

articleTitle: Magnetism of Iron Clusters in Noble Metals
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Effective magnetic moments P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> and spin glass freezing temperatures T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub> were determined by susceptibility measurements for rapidly quenched Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> 0≤x≤10) and Au<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">100-x</sub>Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> (0≤x≤20) alloys. The volume fraction of clusters of Fe atoms in these alloys was estimated by analysis of Mössbauer spectra. On comparing the volume fractions of clusters to P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> and T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>, we obtained the following results. 1) the P<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</sub> of dimers and trimers were estimated to be 6.4 μB and 11.3 μB for the Cu-Fe system, and 7.3 μB and 11.2 μB for the Au-Fe system, respectively. 2) Both the Cu-Fe and the Au-Fe systems exhibited the same freezing temperature, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</sub>, for the same total number of Fe atoms involved in isolated atoms and in clusters, dimer and trimer.

articleTitle: Characteristic of Peak Shift in MR Read Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetoresistive (MR) heads, the characteristics of which do not depend on the medium velocity, are superior to inductive heads at low medium velocities and high recording densities. Because of the nonlinear relation between the applied magnetic field and the magnetoresistance, second harmonic distortion occurs. In this study, the dependence of this second harmonic distortion on the peak shift and error rate was investigated. Intervals between the zero-crossing of a differentiated readout waveform from a two bit pattern were measured using a time counter. The error rate was calculated from the peak shift and standard deviation of zero-crossing point. The peak shift and error rate as functions of the second harmonic distortion were considered assuming a Gaussian noise distribution. It was found that calculations assuming a Gaussian noise distribution correspond to the experimental data.

articleTitle: Runout Characteristics of Flexible Disks by a New Head-Pad Combination Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Runout (dynamic deflection) of both a Co-Cr/permalloy flexible disk A, and a commercialized particulate flexible disk B, both with diameter 3.5", was studied using a disk drive with two pairs of pads arranged in series relative to the disk rotating direction, and with a photometric positioning sensor in place of a single-pole miniature head. In the drive, the radial position of the sensor over the disk was varied between 30 and 37 mm at disk revolution rates ranging from 400 to 1200 rpm, to evaluate the effect of the pad configuration on the runout characteristics. The runout of disk A was suppressed to between 15 and 30 μm, while that of disk B was almost unchanged at more than 60 μm. Stable read/write characteristics of disk A were observed in the high-density region near 70 kfci under a head pressure of 1 gf and runout of about 20 μm.

articleTitle: Development of a Linear Electromagnetic Actuator for Implantable Artifical Heart
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper deals with the configuration, principle of operation, and experimental results concerning a linear pulse motor for an implantable aritificial heart. The linear pulse motor is designed to be as small as possible so as to minimize the space occupied. The mover is made of laminated Permendur sheets 0.35 mm in thickness. The stators are of the same material in orer to maintain a high saturation flux density. the motor develops a thrust of 60 Newtons with an input power of 2.72 Watts. The mass and volume of the motor are 320 g and 56.6 ml. The characteristic values (figures of merit) of the motor are 22.1 N/W, 1.1 N/ml and 0.19 N/g; these values are two to ten times superior to those of ordinary linear pulse motors, because of the use of Permendur sheets and rare-earth magnets (Sm<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">17</inf>).

articleTitle: The Effect of Head-Medium Interaction in Head Field Calculation
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Head field calculations for a single-pole type head were conducted to determine the effect of magnetic interaction between head and medium. We found that the head field was influenced strongly not only by the magnetic properties of the underlayer but by those of the recording layer. We therefore clarified the relationship between the head field and the parameters of the head and medium through calculations which took the magnetic properties of the recording layer into consideration. Moreover, comparison of the head fields of a single-pole type head and a ring head showed that the former is capable of high-density recording even onto a relatively thick recording layer.

articleTitle: Detection of DC Current and Three-Phase Ground Fault Current Using a Ferromagnetic Pipe
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: New methods for detecting DC current and ground fault current in a three-phase power line system are described. Two detectors both utilize the skin effect of conducting current in a ferromagnetic pipe. The detectors have no windings. The DC current detector outputs almost sinusoidal voltage whose amplitude corresponds well to the DC current. The detector has a simplified circuit configuration and short response time. There are no contacts between the DC line and the sense circuit. The ground fault detector breaks down the three-phase power line within three drive-frequency cycles. This paper summarizes those results.

articleTitle: Source Model of Magnetic Fields of Auditory Evoked Brainstem Responses
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The origins of auditory evoked brainstem responses (ABRs) are not fully understood. In the present study we investigate a possible mechanism of ABR occurrence. A source model for ABRs is proposed which simulates, in part, ABR waveforms. Pathways of auditory nerves are represented by a combination of five or six straight lines. Using this simple pathway model, the waveforms and spatial distributions of electrical potentials and magnetic fields are simulated. The results show that electrical potentials change with the dipole orientation. The spatial patterns of electrical potentials and magnetic fields also vary as the dipole orientation changes. The spatial patterns of calculated potentials closely simulate the contour maps of wave V in measured ABRs.

articleTitle: A Study on a New Head-Pad Interface with a Co-Cr Layered Flexible Disk
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: We describe studies of the effect of the medium construction and head pressure on disk deflection suppression, when using discretely positioned upper and lower pads with Co-Cr system flexible disks and a pointed head. We begin with experimental and analytical investigations of the bending rigidity of Co-Cr system media.

articleTitle: Magnetizing Process of Circular Mode in Longitudinal Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The longitudinal magnetic recording process has been simulated using a supercomputer, and was compared with the perpendicular magnetic recording process. The computer simulation was based on a model of curling incoherent magnetization reversal, and employed statistical calculation of the probable magnetization for magnetic particles in the interior of the magnetic layer of the medium. These simulations confirmed that a circular magnetization mode is formed in the medium during high-density recording, causing recording demagnetizing losses, as we predicted qualitatively about twenty years ago.

articleTitle: Composition and Characteristics of Sputtered Co-Cr Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper reports the relation between composition and characteristics of Co-Cr films prepared by dc magnetron sputtering. The compostition of Co-Co films can be controlled by changing the magnetic flux from magnet and solenoid coils. In films with high Cr content, a good c-axis orientation and small in-plane squareness are obtained, while the perpendicular coercivity and saturation magntization are small. The in-plane M-H loop of a Co-30 at% Cr film shows that the film has a large perpendicular anisotrophy beginning from the initial layer.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power System Using an Orthogonal-Core Type Push-Pull Converter and Characteristics of a Push-Pull Parametric Transformer
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The authors earlier proposed an orthogonal-core type push-pull converter. The converter was constructed with a pair of orthogonal-cores whose primary sides were excited by square-wave choppers, and the converter had almost sinusoidal output current and high power factor. In this paper we report a photovoltaic power system using the push-pull converter. The test results obtained in the trial system indicate that the orthogonal-core type push-pull converter can be applicable to a practical photovoltaic power system. As another application, an orthogonal-core type push-pull parametric transformer is also described here. It was experimentally clarified that a low distorted input current and high input power factor are obtained in the push-pull parametric transformer.

articleTitle: Quasi-Periodic Oscillations in a Three Phase Ferro-Resonant Circuit
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: When a three-phase voltage is applied to ferro-resonant circuits connected in a Y-connection, the third harmonic voltage can be obtained in the zero-phase-sequence circuit. Usually, the waveform of this voltage is almost sinusoidal and the oscillation is stable, but under some conditions the voltage changes to a state of quasi-periodic oscillations. This paper deals with the analysis of the mechanism of the quasi-periodic oscillations in a three-phase ferro-resonant circuit.

articleTitle: Magnetic and Magneto-Optical Properties of Co-(Pr, Nd) Artificial Superlattice
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Artificial superlattices of Co-(Pr, Nd) were fabricated on glass substrates using electron beam evaporation. Magnetic properties such as (i) the temperature dependence of saturation magnetization M<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sub>; (ii) the temperature dependence of the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy constant K⊥ and (iii) the wavelength dependence of the polar Kerr rotation angle θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> were systematically investigated. For Co/Pr and Co/Nd artificial superlattices, rare earth atoms within 25 A of the interface were found to be coupled ferromagnetically with Co atoms at 77 K. The K⊥ increases with decreasing artificial period D, for both the Co/Pr and Co/Nd artificial superlattices. The maximum values of K⊥ at 77 K are 10×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and 4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> erg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> for Co/Pr and Co/Nd respectively. The wavelength at which the minimum θ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> is observed shifts from 0.45 μm to 0.65 μm with decreasing artificial period.

articleTitle: Improvement of Performance in Continuously Vacuum Deposited Co-Cr Film by Substrate Treatment
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Dependence of the perpendicular anisotropy of continuously vacuum deposited Co-Cr films on glow discharge treatment of the polymer base film surface, and on the thickness of a Ti underlayer, was investigated. The relation between the film microstructure and the recording characteristics of the Co-Cr film media was also studied. When the polymer film surface was pretreated by glow discharge with Ar gas, the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">keff</sub> of the Co-Cr films decreased, but when H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> gas was used instead of argon, the deterioration of the H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">keff</sub> was negligible. Co-Cr films deposited on a Ti underlayer had a high H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">keff</sub> regardless of the glow discharge treatment conditions. The Ti underlayers had to be more than 40 Å thick in order for the Co-Cr films to have a small Δθ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">50</sub>, around 5 or 6°. The Co-Cr films showed a columnar structure when the Ti underlayer thickness was in the range from 100 to 2000 Å Co-Cr films with a columnar structure yielded a high reproduced voltage.

articleTitle: Control of Magnetic Properties of Electroless Co Alloy Perpendicular Magnetic Anisotropy Films by Catalyzing Process
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Electroless plated Co alloy films for perpendicular magnetic recording media were investigated as a means of controlling magnetic properties by changing the catalyzing process. In thin regions, such as 500 Å thick, a large difference in magnetic properties was evident for films deposited after acid treatment and those prepared with no acid treatment. This was due to the difference in microstructure of the films. In particular, highly crystallized areas appeared in grains deposited after acid treatment. The films deposited after acid treatment had a high perpendicular coercivity H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c ⊥</sub>. This high coercivity turned out to be due to these highly crystallized areas. Grain sizes could be controlled through the acid treatment, which changed the density of active nuclei.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Operating Characteristics of Ion-Implanted Bubble Memory Chips for a 16M-Bit Device
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A test chip using ion-implanted functions for a 16-Mbit bubble memory device has been designed, fabricated and characterized. A new delineation process for ion-implanted tracks using SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> ion-implantation masks is effective for reducing defects in minor loops. As a result, a bias margin of 22 Oe was obtained for minor loop bubble propagation. Test chip operation over a wide temperature range, from -25°C to 80°C, has been realized.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magneto-Optical Spectra in Compositionally-Modulated Multilayered Films
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: This paper presents an interpretation and analysis of experimentally obtained magneto-optical spectra for compositionally modulated multilayered films of transition metal and noble metal layers, such as Fe/Cu. Two possible mechanisms are discussed: (1) the noble metal atoms at interfaces are magnetically polarized by the transition metals and therefore contribute to the magneto-optical spectrum; and (2) the optical constants of multilayered film are different from those of single-layer film, and the Kerr rotation spectrum is effectively altered by the change in optical constants. This analysis clarifies that mechanism (1) does not occur in this case, whereas most of the experimental results can be explained in terms of (2).

articleTitle: An Analysis of the Behavior of a Parametric Induction Motor with Square-Wave Input Voltage
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Operating characteristics of a parametric induction motor with a sinusoidal input voltage were calculated by a magnetic circuit model proposed by the authors. This paper describes an analysis of the behavior of the parametric induction motor with a square-wave input voltage based on this magnetic circuit model. The analytical results of oscillation voltage versus slip relations and load characteristics show good agreement with the experimental results.

articleTitle: Photoinduced Effect on Magnetic Properties of Ion-Implanted YIG Thin Films--Resonance Field Dependence on Annealing Temperature in Hydrogen Atmosphere
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The photoinduced effect studied here is the decrease ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> in the ferromagnetic resonance field of surface spin wave modes in an ion-implanted layer of YIG film during optical illumination. The H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> or He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> implanted films were annealed in a hydrogen gas atmosphere. The results on annealing show various ΔH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> behavior caused by the implanted and diffused hydrogen, and the formation of a large anisotropy in the surface layer of the He<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-implanted films. Proposed models for changes in the chemical reaction between hydrogen and ferrous ions, and the origin of the large anisotropy, are discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetostriction of Amorphous Fe-Y and (Fe-Co)0.8Y0.2 Alloys
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetostriction of Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub> (0.2≤xɤ0.6) and of (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub> Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub> (0≤x≤0.6) alloys has been measured in the temperature range from 20 to 300 K. In Fe-Y alloys, the magnetostriction λ is 2.8×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at 20 K when x=0.2, and decreases monotonically with increasing x and temperature. This magnetostriction in FeY alloys is the smallest among all Fe-based amorphous binary alloys investigated so far. In (Fe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Co<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.8</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.2</sub> alloys λ at room temperature shows a minimum of 1.0×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> at x-0.3, at which the magnetization and coercive force are 125 emu/g and 0.05 Oe respectively.

articleTitle: 3-D Analysis of Magnetic Fields and Verification of Softwares

articleTitle: Cloth-Transformer with Divided Windings and Tension Annealed Amorphous Wire
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Magnetic devices with a cloth structure have a plain shape, large inductance value and large current capacity. By introducing the idea of divided windings, we realized a cloth-transfer which has an arbitrary winding ratio and small stray capacitance between the windings. In order to improve the characteristics of the device, we tried to use both annealed amorphous wire and thinner wire in the device core. The permeability of the amorphous wire is controlled by the tension during annealing. It was suggested that improvement of the frequency characteristics can be achieved by decreasing the wire diameter.

articleTitle: Noise Reduction Characteristics of Current Sensors Using Amorphous Multi-Core Multivibrator with Negative Feedback Loop
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: New small sized high performance current sensors are presented using an amorphous multi-core multivibrator bridge with a negative feedback loop. Serially connected 8 pair cores are set around a conductor with a current I to detect without contact a magnetic field H (=I/2<o;r) cancelling external disturbance fields. Currents of -200 to 200A (-40 to 40 Oe) from DC to 5 kHz are stably detected with an error of less than 0.4% FS and 0.2% FS for non-linearity and hysteresis, and temperature stability of 0.009% FS/°C for -196°C to 200 °C. The cancelling mechanism of external fields in the multi-core arrangement is analyzed for disturbances originating from a conductor current and a magnetic dipole.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Single-Pole Thin Film Head
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The return path core of a single-pole thin film head for perpendicular recording was extended up to the top surface of the head in order to improve the reproducing sensitivity. In this type of head, as the gap length between the main pole and the return path core decreases, the reproducing sensitivity increases, while distortion of the reproduced waveform caused by the contour effect of the return path core increases. We developed a new head, the return path core of which has a waved edge, in order to reduce the distortion of the reproduced waveform. The waved edge was formed by the ion milling process. The azimuth effects of the waved return path on the recording characteristics, reproduced waveform and peak-shift characteristics was investigated through simulations and experiments. The new head has high sensitivity, low waveform distortion, and small peak-shift displacement.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Single Crystals of Fe7Se8 and Co7Se8
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The optical and magneto-optical properties of single crystals of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>, grown by the Bridgman technique, have been studied. Spectra of the normal-incidence reflectivity, magneto-optical Kerr effect, and UPS were measured at room temperature. The diagonal and off-diagonal elements of the conductivity spectra obtained from these measurements showed that the difference in magnetic behavior of Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> and Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf> is caused by the difference in the 3d electron bandwidth just around the Fermi level. It was also found that the contribution of the spin polarization of conduction electrons to the magneto-optical effect is not significant, but that of a band-to-band transition is more effective. We propose a schematic band structure for Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</inf>, and tentatively assign the transitions corresponding to the absorption spectra and the magneto-optical spectra.

articleTitle: Domain Structures of Co-Zr-Nb Amorphous Main-Pole Film and Characteristics of Perpendicular Magnetic Recording
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Domain structures of Co-Zr-Nb amorphous film for use as the main poles of single-pole perpendicular magnetic recording heads have been observed using the Bitter method. A narrower Co-Zr-Nb main pole with a low H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k</inf> showed a disordered domain structure near its tip in the remanent state. This in turn caused low and unstable sensitivity of the narrow-track single-pole head. Rotation magnetization of major domains is dominant in the magnetization of stable main poles. A stable and highly sensitive single-sided single-pole head was obtained by using a shorter main pole with an aspect ratio of about 1; this pole had an ordered and stable domain structure even in the remanent state.

articleTitle: Induced Magnetic Anisotropy of Ferrofluid Frozen in Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The magnetization process of a ferrofluid whose carrier fluid is paraffin was investigated in the temperature range from 77 K to 300 K, as a function of the cooling field intensity and freezing rate. Phase transitions between the liquid and solid states can be simulated by using the ferrofluids as a magnetic probe. A uniaxial magnetic anisotropy was induced by field cooling in frozen ferrofluids. This induced anisotropy decreased with increasing temperature near the melting point, and disappeared at a temperature 30 K above the melting point. In this region rotational hysteresis was observed. The anisotropy constant K near the melting point is described by the equation K=A·exp(ΔE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub>/kT). The value of the activation energy ΔE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</sub> was almost the same as that of ΔE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">η</sub> estimated from the viscosity vs. temperature relation, η ∞ exp(ΔE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">η</sub>/kT).

articleTitle: Characteristics of Temperature Sensitive Magnetic Powders for Soft Heating and Their Application to Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The basic characteristics of a soft heating method utilizing temperature-sensitive magnetic powders were examined. Soft heating has the following advantages: (1) objects for implantation can be formed in any desired shape, and (2) it should be easy to transfer the powder to deep tissue by magnetic induction. However, no magnetic powder has yet been developed which can produce sufficient heat to reach desired temperatures. In order to generate more heat, metal rings were imbedded in a powder, and eddy current losses within them were utilized. The maximum heat was obtained by using rings of optimum resistance and density.

articleTitle: Simulation of Tape Flying Characteristics on VTR Drum Considering In-Plane Stress
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A simulation study by FEM of the deformation of magnetic tape above the VTR drum has been carried out to investigate the tape flying characteristics. Reynolds' equation and the deformation equations of the tape are solved, taking into account the in-plane stress (i.e. geometrical nonlinearity). The validity of this simulation is checked by comparison with the experimental data. Simulations yielded the following results: 1) the flow of lubricant air from the head window causes the tape to depress; 2) the depression grows larger above the rear of the window; and 3) the depression becomes deep and long with increases in the length of the head window.

articleTitle: Some Considerations on the Anomalous Rotating Phenomena of Parametric Induction Motors
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: The parametric induction motor has many excellent features compared with the ordinary single-phase capacitor motor. Since the parametric induction motor utilizes parametric oscillation, anomalous rotating phenomena may occur due to the parametric oscillation of an inappropriate resonance capacitor, machine size and excitation voltage. In this paper, to clarify the instability phenomena, the operating mechanism of the anomalous rotating phenomena was investigated. The results clarified a main cause of the anomalous phenomena. It was also shown that hysteresis of parametric oscillation of voltage changing corresponds qualitatively to hysteresis of rotating speed changing.

articleTitle: Analysis of perpendicular magnetic recording mechanism by finite element analysis combined with medium magnetization model
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: A new program for simulating magnetic write and read processes was developed, incorporating into the finite element method a model of curling mode magnetization in the perpendicular magnetic recording medium. That is, the curling mode was adopted as describing the mechanism of magnetization reversal in the fine crystal grains comprising the Co-Cr recording layer, and the magnetization vector is computed stochastically, with the dispersion in the easy axis of magnetization and the anisotropy field represented by a probability density function. Such finite element analysis simulations incorporating a magnetization model are capable of addressing complex magnetization processes within the recording medium. This method takes into account magnetic interactions between head and medium which depend on saturation in the head and medium soft magnetic layer and on the strength of magnetization in the medium, effects not accounted for by the scalar potential method; it also incorporates magnetization by rotation, which cannot be included in ordinary finite element analysis. As a result, this approach enables highly accurate, quantitative computer simulations of magnetic read and write processes which take into account not only such magnetic properties of the recording medium as the Co-Cr layer coercivity and saturation magnetization, but magnetic properties of the head and the medium backing layer as well, such as permeabilities and saturation flux densities.

articleTitle: Letter to subscribers - What to expect from volume 4
publicationTitle: IEEE Translation Journal on Magnetics in Japan
abstract: Summary form only given. Some changes in the source material to be translated have occurred for various reasons. First, there will no longer be any translations of digests from the Annual Conference on Magnetics in Japan. It has not been possible to translate the large number of these digests on a timely basis, and by mutual agreement with the Magnetics Society of Japan they will no longer be source material for TJMJ. Replacing the digests will be additional articles from the Journal of the Magnetics Society of Japan (Nippon Oyo Jiki Gakkaishi). The first issues of TJMJ Volume 4 will be devoted to translations of articles from the Journal of the Magnetics Society ofJapan (JMJpn), Volume 12, Number 2. Each original publication has been subjected to the review process of the Magnetic Society of Japan, and the quality of the translation will have been reviewed by the TJMJ Associate Editors. Translations will appear roughly in the order of appearance in the original publication subject to the consent of the authors. All articles that have this consent will be translated. Later issues will be devoted to technical reports from the IEICE Technical Report on Magnetic Recording, again subject to prior approval of the author. It is anticipated that all reports released with approval can be translated. Additional material may be translated if resources are available and when suitable agreements have been achieved. It is our hope that future developments will permit complete translations of all issues of TJMJ.
